issues.issue: The design says to replace the guards of the form `stopped && !budget.workLimitReached() && ...` (PackedJoinEnumerator.java:5478-5482, 5978, 6256, 8342-8345, 8377, 8811) with a new `budget.stopped()` (= deadline/resource/unsupported or remaining == 0). Those sites are not loop-stop checks; they throw PackedMemoInvariantException("... DPhyp traversal stopped without a search limit") when the DPhyp receiver stopped for a non-budget reason. The receiver stops exactly when a costing step fails to reserve (costSparseBushyOrientation returns false at PackedJoinEnumerator.java:8431-8432 when tryConsume() fails, and the receiver at :8336-8339 returns `!costSparseBushyOrientation(...)`). Under the non-latching budget an oversized block is refused while `remaining > 0`, so `stopped == true` but `budget.stopped() == false` and the planner throws an invariant exception on a benign refusal (a planning failure, which then lands in the wp3 fail-safe path).
issues.suggestion: Keep the status-flag form (`workLimitReached()` = 'some deterministic work was refused') at every 'stopped without a search limit' invariant site. Only loop-abort sites whose intent is 'no work left' (:4418, 5049, 5097, 6412, 8519, 8753, 8960; PackedIncumbentSearch.java:783, 989, 1016) are candidates for a non-latching predicate, and each must be audited individually because several of them are also the guard that turns a refusal into `return false` instead of a throw (:4418-4422).

issues.issue: PackedSearchBudget.sampleDeadline() (PackedSearchBudget.java:51-60) also returns false once workLimitReached is set (:52), and it is the last conjunct of canBeginMandatoryCompletion (:119-123) and the entry gate of optimizeGreedySeeds (PackedJoinEnumerator.java:11156-11159). The design's list of gates to make arithmetic omits sampleDeadline, so after a refused optional block canBeginMandatoryCompletion would still be false and greedy seeding would still be skipped - the latch survives for the mandatory-completion path the fix is meant to unblock.
issues.suggestion: Include sampleDeadline() in the set of gates that test only deadlineReached/resourceLimitReached/unsupportedSemantics (plus the actual deadline sample). Add a unit case: after a refused 5000-unit block, canBeginMandatoryCompletion(1) and sampleDeadline() are true.

issues.issue: PackedPlanningResult (PackedPlanningResult.java:38-41) throws IllegalArgumentException unless workLimitReached == (status == INCOMPLETE_WORK_LIMIT) and deadlineReached == (status == INCOMPLETE_DEADLINE). PackedCascadesPlanner.java:586-588 passes budget.workLimitReached(), budget.deadlineReached() and budget.completionStatus() separately, and completionStatus() ranks work-limit above deadline (PackedSearchBudget.java:165-170). Today both flags can already become true (tryReserveMandatoryCompletion :91-101 does not check deadlineReached, so deadline -> then an oversized mandatory completion sets workLimitReached), but under the non-latching design it becomes the common case: an early refused optional block sets workLimitReached, the search continues, the deadline is hit later, deadlineReached becomes true, and PackedPlanningResult throws. The design does not reconcile the two legacy flags with the single completion status.
issues.suggestion: Derive the legacy flags from completionStatus at PackedCascadesPlanner.java:587 (workLimitReached = status == INCOMPLETE_WORK_LIMIT, deadlineReached = status == INCOMPLETE_DEADLINE), or define the precedence explicitly in PackedSearchBudget and expose one pair of accessors that agree with completionStatus(). Add a test that refuses an optional block and then expires the deadline.

issues.issue: The finite-ceiling scheme is internally inconsistent and does not deliver what the repro needs. (a) Clamping rows to ROWS_CEILING = 1e100 'before multiplication in joinRows' (PackedJoinEnumerator.java:3659-3668) makes joinRows(1e200, 1e200) == joinRows(1e100, 1e100), contradicting the design's own additional test ('remains > joinRows(1e100, 1e100)'). (b) With inputs of 1e200 rows (PackedPlanningFailSafeReviewReproTest.distinctPlansAcrossInputOrders(1e200)), every 2-way product is 1e400 -> +Inf -> COST_CEILING, so all plans still tie at the ceiling; 3.8.1 alone leaves `saturatedShape.size() > 1` and the whole result rests on 3.8.2. (c) PackedCostNumericContractTest#hugeJoinProductsSaturateInsteadOfOverflowing (PackedCostNumericContractTest.java:30-33) asserts joinRows(1e300, 1e300, *) == Double.MAX_VALUE and will go red; the design's existingTestsAtRisk names PackedPlannerResourceBudgetTest/PackedSearchTest instead, and misses PackedExecutableFallbackTierTest.java:44/159 which assert MAX_VALUE winner costs offered directly to the winner table.
issues.suggestion: Specify the ceilings so that one multiplication of two ceiling values stays below COST_CEILING and strictly above any single ceiling (e.g. ROWS_CEILING = 1e60, COST_CEILING = 1e150), clamp the product (not the inputs) in joinRows, and state explicitly that saturated ties are resolved by 3.8.2, not removed by 3.8.1. Rewrite PackedCostNumericContractTest's saturation cases to the new ceiling and decide whether PackedWinnerTable should also clamp offered costs (PackedExecutableFallbackTierTest offers MAX_VALUE directly).

issues.issue: The design says to sort factor arrays in collectFactors 'and in collectWinnerFactors / the correlated-filter collectors'. All of these funnel into collectStackedFactors (PackedJoinEnumerator.java:11574-11607), and so does collectEmittedPrefixFactors (:11565-11567, forcedJoinWinnerId != 0), which is used at :9623 to recover the *physical* emitted prefix order of a retained winner ('no contribution is attributed to a guessed physical order', :9628-9634). If the sort is implemented in the shared collector, physical prefix contributions are attributed to the wrong factors. Likewise collectPhysicalPrefixRelations (:11513-11520) must stay in physical order.
issues.suggestion: Sort only in collectSelectedFactors/collectFactors (:11486-11506) after collectStackedFactors returns, never inside collectStackedFactors; leave collectEmittedPrefixFactors and collectPhysicalPrefixRelations untouched; audit every caller of collectWinnerFactors (:11508) for positional assumptions before sorting there. Add a test that a resumed/checkpointed prefix reconstruction (planCacheRecostWorkUnits path) is unchanged.

issues.issue: In selectNextTupleExpr (QueryJoinOptimizer.java:984-1026) ranking runs over readyExpressions (:998-1003, SERVICE dependencies), while the design computes component legality over 'the current candidate set'. If the only prefix-connected member of a component is a SERVICE whose service variable is not yet bound, every ready candidate is illegal, `result` stays null and the method hits `assert result != null` / NPE at :1022-1023. Example: prefix {?s}, joinArgs = SERVICE ?svc { ?s :p ?x }, { ?x :q ?y }, { ?z :r ?svc } - all in one component with the prefix, only the SERVICE is directly connected. The design defines no fallback for an empty legal set.
issues.suggestion: Build the union-find over the set that is actually ranked (readyExpressions plus the prefix virtual node); then some prefix-touching member of each prefix-touching component is ready by construction and the legal set is non-empty. Keep an explicit `if (legal.isEmpty()) legal = readyExpressions` fallback and a unit test with a not-ready SERVICE bridge. The pairwise path already has a removeFirst fallback (:547-551).

issues.issue: Sub-item (c) says a right side with rows <= 0 is a certified empty 'when it is exact (new flag or confidence == 1.0)'. That re-introduces exactness-from-confidence, which sub-item (a) removes at JoinFactorCostModel.java:579 and :688; EvidenceProfile.difference already does the same at EvidenceProfile.java:367 (`confidence == 1.0d && right.confidence == 1.0d` = exactMatchCoverage). The design also says semiJoin should 'use the same floor as difference (rows*0.5)'. But difference's handling of an empty right is :360-362 (return `this`, i.e. no rows removed, which is the correct upper bound), while the 0.5 floor at :371-373 is for the 'everything matched' case. Applying a rows*0.5 policy to MINUS-with-uncertain-empty-right would wrongly shrink the estimate.
issues.suggestion: Define exactness solely by the explicit flag (and migrate :367 to it). Specify the uncertain-zero policy per operator: semi-join with an uncertain-empty right -> rows floored (0.5*left or min(1,left) as in LmdbPackedCostModel.java:3141-3143) and confidence = min(left, right.confidence); MINUS with an uncertain-empty right -> keep left rows, only lower confidence; MINUS with 'all matched' uncertain -> keep the existing 0.5 floor. Note BagEstimateMathTest.java:71-77 (semiJoinUsesRhsExistenceWhenThereAreNoSharedVariables) expects rows 0 for an empty right and will need re-deriving.

issues.issue: PackedCostAlgebra.saturatedAdd/saturatedMultiply (PackedCostAlgebra.java:194-203) use comparisons (`left > MAX_VALUE - right`, `value > MAX_VALUE / multiplier`) that are false for NaN, so NaN propagates unclamped; saturatedMultiply also takes a `long multiplier`, a different signature from the PJE/PIS helpers. The design's 'delegate to CostArithmetic' needs to cover NaN sanitisation and both overloads. Also PackedIncumbentSearch.saturatedAdd (:1718-1721) additionally rejects negative sums, unlike the PJE variant (:11651-11654) - the shared helper must pick one contract.
issues.suggestion: Give CostArithmetic explicit NaN handling and both (double,double) and (double,long) overloads; document and test the negative-sum rule once.

issues.issue: UNKNOWN_ROWS_CEILING inside the packed arithmetic helper is effectively dead code: packed leaves never reach saturatedAdd as NaN. PackedIncumbentSearch.java:1600-1605 accepts provider rows only when finite and >= 0, then falls through to relResultSizeEstimate (:1616-1619), EMPTY_SET/SINGLETON (:1620-1625) and statementPatternRows (:1679-1688: 1e6 x 0.01 per bound term). The packed planner's 'unknown' policy therefore lives at :1679-1688, not in saturatedAdd, and the design leaves two different unknown policies (1e9 in CostVector vs 1e6-scaled in packed) without saying so.
issues.suggestion: State that the packed unknown fallback is statementPatternRows and either leave it alone in this WP or route it through the same named constant; do not claim the packed enumerator applies UNKNOWN_ROWS_CEILING.

issues.issue: Changing CostVector.INFINITE (CostVector.java:30-32) to a finite ceiling changes OptimizationGoal's default costBound (OptimizationGoal.java:57, 68, 89) whose hashCode is mixed into LmdbCascadesOptimizer.goalFingerprint (LmdbCascadesOptimizer.java:378-389, :382). Any persisted or cross-run cache keyed on that fingerprint would miss after upgrade; PlanProvenance.java:32 and RejectedAlternative.java:28 also default to INFINITE and are rendered in explain output.
issues.suggestion: Check whether goalFingerprint reaches a persisted cache key; if so bump the cache version. Grep for identity comparisons against CostVector.INFINITE before changing it.

issues.issue: Second commit (paths as run members): connectedByRealBinding (QueryJoinOptimizer.java:1820-1835) and isConnectedToBoundVars (:1646-1656) both use getBindingInfo(x).mayOutput, and getBindingInfo(ArbitraryLengthPath) (:1050-1062) adds the inner path expression's mayOutput. issues.issue: EvidenceProfile is a public record (EvidenceProfile.java:26-29) with 18 internal `new EvidenceProfile(...)` uses plus BagEstimate.java (2) and BindingProfile.java (1); adding an `exact` component changes the canonical constructor and is a public API break unless a compatibility constructor and the 9-argument `EvidenceProfile.of(...)` (:51-53, used by the repro test) are kept. 3.8.1 saturation family in LMDB: LmdbFactorCostAssembler.finiteDifference (LmdbFactorCostAssembler.java:226-229) returns Double.MAX_VALUE for non-finite totals and saturatingAdd/saturatingMultiply live there too; the design mentions adopting CostArithmetic for saturatingMultiply only as shared-infrastructure prose, not as a change in this WP, so LMDB can still inject MAX_VALUE into the packed cost stream.
3.8.6(a) companion: EvidenceProfile.difference's exactMatchCoverage (EvidenceProfile.java:367) is another confidence==1.0 exactness inference and is not in the (a) change list.
semanticRegressionRisks: 3.8.5 (heuristic path, every store): dataset { :s1 :p :x1 . :x1 :q :y1 } with SERVICE <urn:ep> { ?s :p ?x } written first, query `SELECT * { ?z :r ?svc . SERVICE ?svc { ?s :p ?x } . ?x :q ?y }` after an outer prefix binding ?s: with legality computed over all candidates but ranking over readyExpressions, the legal set can be empty and planning fails at QueryJoinOptimizer.java:1022-1023 (query error, not wrong rows). Handled only if components are computed over the ranked set.

3.8.5 (lost sound optimization): prefix `?s a :T` (1e6 rows), candidates `?s :p ?x` (1e6) and `?x :q :const` (1 row, same component, not prefix-connected). The component rule forbids the 1-row pattern before `?s :p ?x` even though 1e6 x 1 followed by an index lookup on both ?s and ?x is the cheaper plan; roadmap 4.4's 'certified-small inputs' exception is dropped, so develop's cost-first plan is lost here (parity with the packed planner, which also has no such edge unless the factor is access-enabling).

3.8.6(c): `SELECT ?s { ?s :p ?o FILTER EXISTS { ?s :q ?m } }` over { :a :p 1 . :b :p 2 } (no :q triples) - a heuristic empty right now yields rows = 0.5*left instead of 0, which can flip the packed semi-join strategy choice; results are unaffected but PackedSearch/LMDB plan-shape tests for EXISTS over an empty predicate may move.

3.8.6(a): fewer estimates carry DATABASE_EXACT, so LEO learning can now correct cardinalities it previously froze; per the cross-query poisoning history this can also re-open feedback pollution for estimates that were exact-by-confidence only, so the LmdbEstimateClassification.databaseExact sources (lmdb-exact, finite-values, quad-total) must be shown to still stamp DATABASE_EXACT.

3.8.1 EstimateVector.filter clamp: a pass ratio of exactly 0 with no passInterval yields lower = upper = 0 under both old and new code; if any consumer treats a [0,0] interval as certified empty, a heuristic zero-pass filter becomes an exact zero - keep an epsilon floor or carry the confidence.
